transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Charles Snyder.
The Supreme Court is wrestling with whether a case seeking damages over the costs of climate
change should be allowed to proceed.
NPR's Kerry Johnson reports on the first arguments of the new term at the High Court.
Boulder, Colorado sued Suncor and ExxonMobil to recover money for the costs of responding
to global warming.
That was back in 2018, but the case has still not reached a jury.
County officials argued the companies knew but chose to deceive the public about the
threats from climate change.
The energy giants are asking the Supreme Court to block the lawsuit because they say the
federal government should be in charge of such a sweeping issue.
The justices asked tough questions of both sides.
They seem to be weighing a potential flood of cases in state courts against blocking
cases by Boulder and other local governments at such an early stage.
Kerry Johnson, NPR News.
At his rally in Nebraska, President Trump rolled out a new tax exemption for diesel
fuel, signing an executive order to ease limits on the tax-free use of red-dye diesel.
Trump was campaigning for Republican Senator Pete Ricketts, who was locked in a competitive
contest with independent Dan Osborn.
Time is running out for eligible voters to register for next month's midterm elections
in some parts of the country, and Paris-Hansi Lo Wang reports that election officials recommend
those already registered to pay close attention to any further deadlines.
Today is the last chance for eligible voters to register or update their registration in
American Samoa, Arizona, Indiana, and Ohio, plus many southern states, including Arkansas,
Florida, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Texas.
And later this week, there are more voter registration deadlines for the midterm elections.
Missouri closes registration this Wednesday, Oklahoma's deadline is Friday, and sign-ups
in Delaware and Saturday.
If you're already registered, you can confirm your status by visiting your state or territory's
official election website.
Election officials recommend checking before the deadline, especially if you recently moved,
changed your name, or haven't voted in a while.
Hansi Lo Wang, NPR News.
President Trump says he will pay for those controversial television ads that praise him.
NPR's Franco Ordonia's reports that taxpayers have been footing the bill for the ads.
President Trump announced the new plan amid ongoing backlash over the publicly funded
spots running ahead of the midterms.
Trump defended the ads via his social media page, arguing that it was standard practice,
and that he was promoting the USA and, quote, paying for them with USA money.
And critics say the pro-Trump ads are blatantly partisan, and you use Republican talking points.
Trump says that he and his political action committee are taking over payment of the ads.
Franco Ordonia's, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Students at the Ivy League Cornell University rallied on campus Monday, demanding tougher
action against sexual violence on campus, they packed into a plaza to protest the university's
response to a classmate's gang rape allegations.
They demanded an outside investigation and called for the resignation of University President
Michael Kotlikoff, a former music pastor in Ohio, who appeared briefly on American Idol
has been sentenced to life in prison without parole.
40-year-old Caleb Flynn was convicted by a jury last week for murdering his wife while
he was having an affair.
The American Academy of Pediatrics, warning that unpasteurized milk and other raw dairy
foods are unsafe to eat and can cause serious illness, NPR's Maria Godoy reports on a new
policy statement from the group that says the risks are especially high for young children
and people who are pregnant or breastfeeding.
The updated guidance from the AAP calls for a ban on the sale and distribution of raw
milk and dairy products, including raw cheeses, because they can cause life-threatening infections.
While advocates of raw milk products say they offer health benefits, these claims are not
backed by scientific evidence.
Unpasteurized dairy products can harbor pathogens like listeria, avian flu, and salmonella.
This year, an outbreak of E. coli linked to raw milk cheeses resulted in 13 illnesses,
including eight hospitalizations.
More than half of the people sickened were children under five years of age.
Three people developed severe kidney damage.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.

topics.text: Supreme Court hears arguments on whether Boulder, Colorado climate damages lawsuit against oil companies can proceed
President Trump signs executive order easing tax limits on red-dye diesel fuel at Nebraska rally
Election officials remind voters of voter registration deadlines in multiple states ahead of midterm elections
President Trump announces he will pay for controversial pro-Trump television ads previously funded by taxpayers
Cornell University students rally demanding investigation and president's resignation over sexual violence response
Ohio man Caleb Flynn sentenced to life in prison for murdering wife during affair
American Academy of Pediatrics warns raw milk and dairy products pose serious health risks to children
